topicCards.title: President's Medals for Distinguished and Meritorious Service

keyFacts.title: Delhi Police Honours
keyFacts.desc: Delhi Police received 17 medals, including 2 President's Medals for Distinguished Service (PSM). Additional Commissioner of Police Dinesh Kumar Gupta (2010-batch IPS) was among the PSM awardees.

keyFacts.title: Karnataka Honours
keyFacts.desc: The 22 officers from Karnataka included personnel from Police, Fire & Emergency Services, and Home Guard & Civil Defence departments.

staticGkPoints: President's Police Medal for Gallantry (PPMG) and President's Police Medal for Distinguished Service (PPMDS) are among the highest police honours in India.
The President's Police Medal was instituted on March 1, 1951, by the President of India.
Medals are awarded for Gallantry, Distinguished Service, and Meritorious Service, with different criteria for each.
The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) is responsible for the administration of these awards.

topicCards.title: Parliamentary Panel Flags Slow Pace of Manuscript Digitisation

keyFacts.title: Concern Raised
keyFacts.desc: A parliamentary panel has expressed serious concern over the slow rate of digitisation of manuscripts in India.

keyFacts.title: Gyan Bharatam Mission
keyFacts.desc: The mission had set an ambitious target of digitising one crore (10 million) manuscripts by 2030.

keyFacts.title: Current Progress
keyFacts.desc: So far, only 7.5 lakh (0.75 million) texts have been digitised, indicating a significant shortfall against the target.

keyFacts.title: Significance
keyFacts.desc: Manuscripts are invaluable cultural heritage, and their digitisation is crucial for preservation, accessibility, and research.

staticGkPoints: The National Mission for Manuscripts (NMM) was established in 2003 by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India.
NMM aims to identify, document, conserve, and make accessible the manuscript wealth of India.
India is estimated to have over 10 million manuscripts, making it one of the largest repositories globally.
The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), also under the Ministry of Culture, is responsible for archaeological research and protection of cultural heritage.
examinerPerspective: Questions can link the mission to cultural heritage, digital India initiatives, and government accountability.
Focus on the objectives of the National Mission for Manuscripts and its parent ministry.
Comparison of targets vs. achievements is a common theme in governance-related questions.
UPSC might ask about the challenges in manuscript preservation and digitisation.

examRelevance.note: Government schemes, cultural institutions, and heritage preservation.
Direct questions on NMM, its establishment, and objectives.
Relevance to state-specific manuscript collections and preservation efforts.

keyFacts.desc: This is a significant social welfare initiative by the Government of Kerala, reflecting its commitment to inclusive social security.

The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) in the Indian Constitution (Part IV) guide states to secure social and economic justice.

topicCards.title: Osprey Reintroduction Project in Southern England Succeeds

keyFacts.title: Species Reintroduction
keyFacts.desc: Conservationists successfully reintroduced ospreys to Dorset, England, after a century-long absence, with breeding observed for the first time since 1847.

keyFacts.title: Project Origin
keyFacts.desc: The project began in 2017, moving young ospreys from Scotland to Dorset to establish a new population.

keyFacts.title: Rapid Expansion
keyFacts.desc: A study highlights that pioneering pairs are crucial for rapid species expansion into new territories, establishing separate breeding groups and accelerating population growth.

keyFacts.title: Conservation Impact
keyFacts.desc: Translocation projects like this create 'artificial pioneers,' saving decades of natural recolonisation time and connecting new osprey populations with established areas.

staticGkPoints: Ospreys (Pandion haliaetus) are fish-eating birds of prey found worldwide, often indicators of healthy aquatic ecosystems.
Species reintroduction is a key conservation strategy to restore populations in areas where they have become extinct.
The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Red List categorizes species based on their extinction risk.
CITES (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora) regulates international trade in endangered species.
examinerPerspective: UPSC often asks about conservation efforts, endangered species, and international conventions like IUCN and CITES.
Questions might focus on the methods of species reintroduction and their ecological impact.
Understanding the role of 'pioneering pairs' in population dynamics is important.
This news highlights successful conservation models that can be applied elsewhere.

examRelevance.note: Biodiversity, conservation projects, endangered species, environmental organizations.

topicCards.title: India, Russia Discuss Deeper Cooperation on Northern Sea Route

keyFacts.title: Bilateral Talks
keyFacts.desc: India and Russia are engaged in discussions to deepen cooperation on the Northern Sea Route (NSR).

keyFacts.title: Arctic Trade Push
keyFacts.desc: Moscow is actively developing the Arctic corridor as a major Europe-Asia trade link, leveraging melting Arctic ice.

keyFacts.title: Strategic Importance
keyFacts.desc: The NSR offers a significantly shorter maritime route between Europe and Asia compared to the Suez Canal, reducing transit times and costs.

keyFacts.title: India's Interest
keyFacts.desc: India is exploring connectivity opportunities and potential benefits from this route for its trade and strategic interests.

staticGkPoints: The Northern Sea Route (NSR) is a shipping lane officially defined by Russian law as running along the Russian Arctic coast from the Kara Sea to the Bering Strait.
The Arctic Council is the leading intergovernmental forum promoting cooperation, coordination, and interaction among the Arctic states and indigenous communities.
India holds Observer status in the Arctic Council since 2013 and released its Arctic Policy in 2022.
The melting of Arctic ice due to climate change is making the NSR more accessible, raising both economic opportunities and environmental concerns.
examinerPerspective: UPSC frequently asks about India's foreign policy, strategic partnerships, and geopolitical developments like Arctic routes.
Questions may cover the geographical significance of NSR, its economic implications, and environmental challenges.

topicCards.title: Genetic Basis of Redback Spider's Unique Mating Somersault

keyFacts.title: Unique Behavior
keyFacts.desc: Male redback spiders perform a somersault directly towards the female's fangs during mating, a behavior crucial for reproduction.

keyFacts.title: Genetic Control
keyFacts.desc: Recent research indicates that a singular genetic region governs this intricate somersaulting behavior.

keyFacts.title: Inheritance Pattern
keyFacts.desc: This fascinating behavior is inherited through the X chromosome, and experimental hybrids suggest it is recessive and X-linked.

keyFacts.title: Challenging Views
keyFacts.desc: Conversely, abdominal narrowing in these spiders appears influenced by multiple genes and environmental conditions, challenging traditional views on genetic trait complexity.

staticGkPoints: Redback spiders (Latrodectus hasselti) are venomous spiders native to Australia, belonging to the genus Latrodectus (widow spiders).
Sexual cannibalism, where the female eats the male during or after mating, is common in redback spiders.
X-linked inheritance refers to the inheritance of genes located on the X chromosome, often showing different patterns in males and females.
Genetics is the study of heredity and the variation of inherited characteristics, a fundamental branch of biology.
examinerPerspective: UPSC and other exams can ask about animal behavior, genetics, and specific biological phenomena.
Questions might focus on the concept of X-linked inheritance or the complexity of genetic traits.
Understanding the evolutionary reasons behind such seemingly risky mating behaviors (e.g., increased paternity success) is important.
This news highlights advancements in understanding genetic control of complex behaviors.

examRelevance.note: General science (biology, genetics, animal kingdom).
Basic biology, scientific discoveries.
General science, zoology.

topicCards.title: Kerala Schools' Independence Day Circular Omits Vande Mataram Directive

keyFacts.title: Circular Content
keyFacts.desc: The Director of General Education in Kerala issued a circular to school head teachers for Independence Day, mentioning only the national anthem, 'Jana Gana Mana'.

keyFacts.title: Omission
keyFacts.desc: The circular did not include any directive to sing 'Vande Mataram' during the Independence Day celebrations in schools.

keyFacts.title: National Symbols
keyFacts.desc: 'Jana Gana Mana' is India's National Anthem, while 'Vande Mataram' is the National Song.

keyFacts.title: State Context
keyFacts.desc: This decision by the Kerala government highlights the ongoing discussions and interpretations regarding the mandatory singing of national symbols in educational institutions.

staticGkPoints: 'Vande Mataram' was composed by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay in 1876 and was first sung in a political session of the Indian National Congress in 1896.
It was adopted as the National Song of India on January 24, 1950, the same day 'Jana Gana Mana' was adopted as the National Anthem.
The National Anthem, 'Jana Gana Mana', was composed by Rabindranath Tagore and first publicly sung in 1911.
Article 51A(a) of the Indian Constitution states that it is the duty of every citizen to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem.
examinerPerspective: This topic links to national symbols, constitutional provisions (Fundamental Duties), and cultural practices.
Examiners often test the distinction between National Anthem and National Song, their composers, and adoption dates.

topicCards.title: Centre Scraps 20-Year-Old 12-Minute Cap on TV Ad Breaks

keyFacts.title: Regulatory Change
keyFacts.desc: The Ministry of Information & Broadcasting (I&B) has scrapped the 20-year-old rule that capped TV ad breaks at 12 minutes per hour.

keyFacts.title: Previous Rule
keyFacts.desc: The 12-minute cap was introduced in 2006, aiming to regulate advertising time on television channels.

keyFacts.title: Reason for Change
keyFacts.desc: The I&B Ministry argued that the television landscape has drastically evolved, rendering the 2006 rule obsolete in the current media environment.

keyFacts.title: Impact
keyFacts.desc: This decision is expected to lead to longer ad breaks on television, potentially impacting viewer experience and broadcasters' revenue models.

staticGkPoints: The Ministry of Information & Broadcasting (I&B) is responsible for the formulation and administration of rules, regulations, and laws relating to information, broadcasting, press, and films in India.
The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) is the independent regulator for the telecommunications sector in India, but the ad cap was under I&B.
The Cable Television Networks (Regulation) Act, 1995, provides the framework for regulating cable television networks in India.
Media regulation in India involves balancing commercial interests, public interest, and technological advancements.
examinerPerspective: Questions can focus on the role of the I&B Ministry, media regulation, and the impact of policy changes on the broadcasting sector.
Understanding the historical context of the 2006 rule and the reasons for its repeal is important.

keyFacts.title: Objective

keyFacts.title: Initiation
keyFacts.desc: This day was officially declared by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2021.

staticGkPoints: The partition of India occurred in 1947, dividing British India into two independent dominions: India and Pakistan.
The partition led to one of the largest mass migrations in human history, accompanied by widespread violence and loss of life.
Lord Mountbatten was the last Viceroy of India and oversaw the partition process.
The Radcliffe Line demarcated the boundaries between India and Pakistan.

topicCards.title: Preserving India's Written Heritage: Manuscript Digitisation Efforts

keyFacts.title: Cultural Significance
keyFacts.desc: Manuscripts represent an invaluable part of India's rich written heritage, encompassing diverse languages, scripts, and subjects.

keyFacts.title: Digitisation Goal
keyFacts.desc: The Gyan Bharatam Mission aimed to digitise one crore manuscripts by 2030 to ensure their preservation and global accessibility.

keyFacts.title: Current Challenge
keyFacts.desc: A parliamentary panel highlighted that only 7.5 lakh manuscripts have been digitised so far, indicating a significant gap in achieving the target.

keyFacts.title: Preservation Need
keyFacts.desc: Digitisation helps protect fragile physical manuscripts from decay, natural disasters, and ensures their availability for future generations of scholars and the public.

staticGkPoints: The National Mission for Manuscripts (NMM) was launched in 2003 by the Ministry of Culture to conserve and make accessible India's vast manuscript wealth.
India is home to an estimated 5 million manuscripts, making it one of the largest repositories of manuscript heritage in the world.
UNESCO's 'Memory of the World Programme' aims to preserve and provide access to documentary heritage of universal value.
The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) is the premier organization for archaeological research and protection of cultural heritage in India.
examinerPerspective: This topic links cultural heritage preservation with modern technology and government initiatives.
Questions may focus on the importance of manuscripts, the objectives of NMM, and the challenges in heritage conservation.
UPSC might ask about the role of digital technologies in preserving cultural heritage and the broader implications for research and education.
Static GK on cultural institutions and international heritage programs is relevant.

mcqData.q: Which of the following medals are typically announced on the eve of Republic Day and Independence Day to recognize exemplary service by police and other uniformed personnel?
mcqData.explanation: The President's Police Medal (and its variants like President's Police Medal for Gallantry, Distinguished Service, and Meritorious Service) are specifically awarded to police, fire, home guard, and other uniformed personnel on the eve of Republic Day and Independence Day. Bharat Ratna and Padma Vibhushan are civilian awards, while Param Vir Chakra is a military gallantry award.

mcqData.q: The 'Gyan Bharatam Mission', which aims for the digitisation of manuscripts, is associated with which Union Ministry?
mcqData.explanation: The National Mission for Manuscripts (NMM), under which initiatives like 'Gyan Bharatam Mission' for digitisation fall, was established by the Ministry of Culture. Its primary objective is to conserve and make accessible India's vast manuscript wealth.

mcqData.q: The 'Aswasakiranam scheme', which provides caregiver assistance, is an initiative of which Indian state?
mcqData.explanation: The Aswasakiranam scheme, which recently saw an increase in caregiver assistance to ₹1,000, is a social welfare initiative of the Government of Kerala. It supports caregivers of chronically bedridden, disabled, or terminally ill persons.

mcqData.q: The recent successful reintroduction of Ospreys to Dorset, England, after a century-long absence, is an example of which conservation strategy?
mcqData.explanation: The reintroduction of Ospreys by moving young birds from Scotland to Dorset is an example of species translocation, a conservation strategy involving the movement of living organisms from one area with a healthy population to another where the species has been extirpated or is endangered.

mcqData.q: India and Russia are discussing deeper cooperation on the Northern Sea Route. Which of the following statements about the Northern Sea Route (NSR) is correct?
opts: It primarily connects the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans via the Panama Canal.
It runs along the Russian Arctic coast, offering a shorter route between Europe and Asia.
It is entirely located within the territorial waters of Canada.
It is a freshwater route through Siberia.
mcqData.explanation: The Northern Sea Route (NSR) is a shipping lane along the Russian Arctic coast, offering a significantly shorter maritime route between Europe and Asia compared to traditional routes like the Suez Canal. It is not related to the Panama Canal or Canada's territorial waters, nor is it a freshwater route.

mcqData.q: The unique somersaulting mating behavior of male redback spiders has been found to be primarily governed by a singular genetic region inherited through which chromosome?
mcqData.explanation: Recent research indicates that the intricate somersaulting behavior of male redback spiders during mating is governed by a singular genetic region inherited through the X chromosome, and it is a recessive, X-linked trait.

mcqData.q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes between 'Jana Gana Mana' and 'Vande Mataram' in the context of India's national symbols?
opts: 'Jana Gana Mana' is the National Song, and 'Vande Mataram' is the National Anthem.
Both 'Jana Gana Mana' and 'Vande Mataram' are National Anthems.
'Jana Gana Mana' is the National Anthem, and 'Vande Mataram' is the National Song.
Neither has official national symbol status.
mcqData.explanation: 'Jana Gana Mana' is India's National Anthem, composed by Rabindranath Tagore. 'Vande Mataram', composed by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, is India's National Song. Both were adopted on January 24, 1950, but have distinct statuses.

mcqData.q: The Ministry of Information & Broadcasting recently scrapped the 20-year-old cap on TV ad breaks. What was the duration of this cap per hour?
mcqData.explanation: The Centre scrapped the 20-year-old rule that capped TV ad breaks at 12 minutes per hour. This rule was introduced in 2006 by the I&B Ministry.

mcqData.q: Partition Horrors Remembrance Day is observed annually on which date?
mcqData.explanation: Partition Horrors Remembrance Day is observed annually on August 14th to commemorate the victims and suffering caused by the partition of India in 1947. It was officially declared by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2021.

mcqData.q: Deepika Kumari, a prominent Indian athlete, is associated with which sport?
mcqData.explanation: Deepika Kumari is a renowned Indian professional archer, specializing in the recurve event. She has won multiple medals at international competitions, including the Archery World Cup.

mcqData.q: The National Commission for Women (NCW) was established as a statutory body in which year?
mcqData.explanation: The National Commission for Women (NCW) was set up as a statutory body in January 1992 under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990. It works to protect and promote the interests of women in India.

mcqData.q: Which of the following is the second-highest literary honour in India, conferred annually by the Sahitya Akademi?
mcqData.explanation: The Sahitya Akademi Award is the second-highest literary honour in India, established in 1954. The Jnanpith Award, established in 1961, is considered the highest literary award in India.

mcqData.q: The National Mission for Manuscripts (NMM) was launched by the Ministry of Culture with the primary objective of:
opts: Promoting modern art forms in India.
Conserving and making accessible India's vast manuscript wealth.
Establishing new museums across the country.
mcqData.explanation: The National Mission for Manuscripts (NMM), launched in 2003 by the Ministry of Culture, aims to identify, document, conserve, and make accessible the manuscript wealth of India. While digitisation is a part of this, the broader objective is conservation and accessibility of manuscripts, not archaeological sites or modern art.

mainsQuestions.q: Discuss the significance of the Northern Sea Route (NSR) for global trade and geopolitics. How does India's engagement with Russia on this route align with its strategic interests and Arctic policy?
mainsQuestions.hint: Key angles: NSR's geographical advantage & economic benefits → Geopolitical implications (Russia's push, Arctic Council) → India's Arctic policy objectives → Benefits for India (trade, energy security, strategic presence) → Challenges and environmental concerns.

mainsQuestions.q: The slow pace of manuscript digitisation, as flagged by a parliamentary panel, raises concerns about the preservation of India's cultural heritage. Critically examine the challenges in preserving India's written heritage and suggest measures to accelerate digitisation efforts.
mainsQuestions.hint: Key angles: Importance of manuscripts as heritage → Challenges (funding, expertise, infrastructure, access, awareness, condition of manuscripts) → Role of National Mission for Manuscripts → Suggestions (public-private partnerships, technology adoption, capacity building, policy reforms, international collaboration).

mainsQuestions.q: In light of the Kerala government's circular regarding national symbols, discuss the constitutional provisions and judicial interpretations concerning the singing of 'Vande Mataram' and 'Jana Gana Mana' in educational institutions.
mainsQuestions.hint: Key angles: Status of National Anthem vs. National Song → Article 51A (Fundamental Duties) → Supreme Court rulings on compulsory singing (Bijoe Emmanuel case) → Balancing national pride with individual rights → Role of state directives.
